Hi Sara / team —

Thanks for the clear questions. Below are concrete answers we can include in contractual language; happy to jump on a quick call with your security engineers if needed. 

1) Training opt-out (binding behavior) 
- When opt-out is enabled (per-account or per-environment), Redwood marks all incoming inputs and generated outputs as "do-not-train" in our ingestion pipeline and excludes them from any dataset pipelines used for model training or fine-tuning.
- This exclusion is enforced at the ingestion service and at dataset assembly; we maintain audit logs proving the exclusion for compliance requests.
- Contract clause suggestion: "Redwood will not use Customer Data marked as "do-not-train" to train, fine-tune, or improve models, internal or external, for any purpose without explicit written permission from Customer."

2) Data residency and storage 
- We support region scoping for stored artifacts. For your account we can scope persisted logs and any trace artifacts to us-east-1. Ephemeral inference processing may touch nearest compute but persisted storage (logs, KV cache dumps, retained prompts) will be kept in us-east-1 as requested.
- Default retention for request/response logs: 30 days.
- Audit logs (access records, policy changes): retained 365 days by default; retention can be shortened via a signed request and a configuration change on Dedicated/Private deployments.

3) PII handling and redaction 
- Redwood provides a PII detection library and a server-side redaction pipeline. We recommend customers do upstream redaction for the highest assurance, but we can enable automatic PII detection to mask or redact fields before persistence. Options: mask (replace with <REDACTED>), remove field, or hash.

4) Auditability & evidence 
- We can produce an export of ingestion flags (with timestamps) showing which records were flagged do-not-train. We can also provide signed attestations for opt-out periods on enterprise contracts.

Attachments: redwood-data-processing-terms.pdf (contains standard DPA language); training-opt-out-form.docx (one-page sign-off)

If you want a compact addendum clause for your legal team, use the sentence above under (1) — we can also embed in a DPA exhibit.

Cheers,
